newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Motta sees possible rate revamp in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Motta sees possible rate revamp in 1997.

text.p: Brazilian Communications Minister Sergio Motta said the government will study a possible telecommunications rate restructuring in 1997 to eliminate cross subsidies before the sector is privatized.
"Cross subsidies make any privatization impossible," Motta told reporters at a press conference.
"Obviously, this will be discussed in 1997 but we have no studies on it as yet," he added.
The government held an initial round of rate rebalancing last November and the market has been awaiting the announcement of a second round in early 1997.
Motta said that any adjustment will not result in a net increase in telecommunications tariffs to phone users.
"I can guarantee that in the mix (of services) there will be no increase in price," he added.
Motta called the news conference to explain and answer questions on a new telecommunications law sent to Congress on Thursday.
The law would create a regulatory watchdog, set broad guidelines for the sector and authorize the break-up and sale of Telebras, the federal telecommunications giant.
